Job title:  Podiatrist 

  Job type:  Full time or part time 

  Salary offer:  Competitive salary offer (DOE) 

   

  About the company:   

 Our client is a locally owned, community-focused podiatry practice with three modern clinics across Albury, Wodonga and Beechworth. Their team is passionate about delivering exceptional patient care while providing a workplace where podiatrists feel supported, valued and able to thrive. 

 They believe high-quality podiatry starts with a healthy, positive working environment. Preventing burnout is a core priority—every practitioner is given ample time, autonomy and support to provide thorough, patient-centred care. 

 There is no “five-minute medicine” here. Generous consultation times, fully digital systems and strong administrative support ensure podiatrists can focus on what they do best—helping patients. 

 Their clinics are equipped with industry-leading tools such as dermatoscopes, shockwave therapy, automated vascular assessment systems, a full strength and conditioning set-up and Structure Scanner 3D orthotic scanning. Each clinic is designed with ergonomics and practitioner safety in mind to support long-term comfort and sustainability. 

 The culture is professional, kind, collaborative and grounded in mutual respect, with a strong commitment to ongoing education and teamwork. 

   

  About the role:  

 As a Podiatrist, you will deliver high-quality, unrushed and patient-centred care supported by longer consultation times. Working within a fully digital clinical environment, you’ll be supported by skilled administrative staff who help streamline your day and reduce unnecessary stress. 

 You’ll have access to premium equipment including dermatoscopes, shockwave therapy, Structure Scanner 3D orthotic scanning, automated vascular systems, and strength and conditioning tools. You’ll also benefit from fully funded in-house CPD and be part of an experienced, supportive clinical team. 

   

  Benefits:   

  A genuine work-life balance  

 
	 Flexible working hours tailored to your lifestyle and family needs 
	 Optional RDO (Rostered Day Off) 
	 No weekend work 
	 No public holiday work 
 

  Supportive team environment  

 
	 Strong administrative support to reduce workload 
	 Positive, collaborative team culture built on open communication 
	 Commitment to preventing burnout and supporting long-term wellbeing 
	 Clinics designed with practitioner safety, comfort and ergonomics in mind 
 

  Professional development & growth  

 
	 Fully funded in-house CPD to meet governing body requirements 
	 Regular clinical discussions, mentoring and shared learning 
	 Exposure to varied caseloads: biomechanics, diabetes care, paediatrics, NDIS and aged care

 Department of Health

Position details

Permanent, part-time

South

Millbrook Rise, 3 Hobart Road


 

 
Job description:

 
Join a supportive, recovery-focused mental health team and help people build meaningful, independent lives. Work collaboratively with consumers, families and healthcare professionals to deliver therapeutic programs and support individual recovery journeys.

 

 






 

The Team:

Millbrook Rise Centre is a 27-bed mental health subacute inpatient facility; we are a consumer-centred service with a focus on rehabilitation and recovery located in the beautiful Derwent Valley. We work closely with various services within not only Statewide Mental Health Services (SMHS) but also with the wider community services such as NDIS providers. 

We are a collaborative team that works with our consumers, their friends and families in their individualised recovery journey. We have a constantly developing activities and therapeutic groups program and we welcome new staff and new ideas to contribute to the activities program at the site.

The Role:

Works collaboratively with clients, other health care providers, stakeholder, families of clients and their carers in the delivery of therapeutic and-or occupational therapy programs 

You will need

Demonstrated capacity to work with people with mental illness and knowledge of client rehabilitation needs, client centred practice and the need to establish an environment of support.

Knowledge of resources and services available to support people with mental illness in the broader community, or the ability to quickly acquire this knowledge.

Demonstrated understanding of the principles of maintaining appropriate therapeutic relationships with clients.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Why Tasmania:

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania's public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

Details of appointment:

Permanent part time, day worker position, working 30.4 hours per fortnight, commencing as soon as possible.

*Notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary: $70,033 to $75,114 per annum (Pro rata). Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary range is in accordance with Public Sector Unions Wages Agreement 2025 

Salary Packaging:

You'll have access to salary package a range of benefits including living expenses up to $9,010 + $2,650 in meal entertainment each FBT year + other benefits if eligible. 

Benefits available to eligible candidates:

A range of leave entitlements, including study leave and Professional Development Support.

Fitness Passport - You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $14.50 per week per person, or $28.05 for a family.

More information about our Employee Benefits can be found here

Successful applicants will be required to meet the essential criteria.

Where there's life, there's Mercy. 

Where there's care, there's You.

Through the battles and the breakthroughs, we're there. Where will you be?

For over a century, our incredible teams have provided care for people when they need it most. Our people feel great pride in this, and they value the security and stability we offer. But it also means so much opportunity - to build on all that's gone before, to grow your impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

As a for-purpose organisation with over 10,000 dedicated, compassionate people, we continue to offer more services and deeper care than ever before. With Mercy, you'll have the chance to make an impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

At Mercy Health, it's all about taking what we have and making it better. 

To do that, we need you. 

Join us at Mercy Health, and help our teams deliver even greater outcomes. 

About the opportunity

Mercy Perinatal is an international centre of excellence in the care of pregnant women and newborns, based at Mercy Hospital for Women and affiliated with The University of Melbourne. You will join a small, passionate and high-performing team of clinicians, administrators, and researchers, playing a key role in shaping our digital presence, showcasing world-class education and research, and deepening engagement with our consumer network (MaPLE).

Provide operational and administrative support across digital media, events, communications and consumer engagement to deliver Mercy Perinatal's education, research and clinical activities.

Plan, create and schedule digital content (including social media, web and podcasts) and support the promotion and delivery of key educational events.

Collaborate with Mercy Perinatal leaders, clinicians, researchers and consumers to support the MaPLE Network and ensure effective, high-quality engagement.

What you'll bring
 

You're resilient, compassionate and have a whole lot of heart. Most importantly, you are committed to delivering exceptional patient-centred care.

To thrive in this role, you will have:

Demonstrated experience in marketing and communications (including digital channels), with excellent written and verbal communication skills, creativity and attention to detail.

Well-developed project and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise, work autonomously, meet deadlines and work flexibly.

The ability to nurture friendly, respectful relationships and contribute to a collaborative team environment.

You will also be required to provide evidence of, or in the process of obtaining:

A current Police Record Check and Working with Children Check.

Proof of current influenza vaccination and other vaccination status consistent with public health orders.

Position Type: Full Time

Employer Name: TJAJH Enterprises Pty Ltd - T/a Mister Minh
A.B.N. 61 685 765 593
Job Location: 350 Bridge Road, Richmond, VIC, 3121,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 28 days - 24 Jul 2026 > 21 Aug 2026

Please include Reference: J1710-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

About the Business
Our client, TJAJH Enterprises Pty Ltd, trades as Mister Minh and operates a fully licensed Vietnamese restaurant at 350 Bridge Road, Richmond, Victoria. The established venue provides dine-in dining, event catering and private function services, with indoor dining, alfresco seating and a dedicated private room for group events. The restaurant is licensed to serve alcohol and also permits BYO wine.

Mister Minh specialises in Vietnamese cuisine and contemporary casual dining, offering a varied menu that includes grilled meats, stir-fried dishes, soups, noodle and rice meals, salads, seafood and house-made sauces. The restaurant is particularly known for its signature smoky barbecue sauce and proprietary marinades, which contribute to its distinctive flavour and dining experience.

The restaurant’s kitchen operations involve ingredient preparation, marinating, portioning, grilling, steaming, frying, simmering, plating, stock rotation and quality control. These processes are supported by established food safety, hygiene and temperature-control procedures to ensure consistent standards across everyday dining, takeaway orders, catered events and private functions.

Through its established Richmond premises, structured restaurant operations and ongoing customer service activities, Mister Minh provides a professional and active hospitality environment for employees seeking to develop their experience within a busy Vietnamese restaurant.

Further information about the restaurant is available at: https://www.misterminh.com/

About the Position
Our client is seeking to appoint a reliable and dedicated full-time Cook to join the kitchen team at Mister Minh. The successful applicant will have a positive attitude, sound cooking skills and at least three years of relevant commercial kitchen experience.

Reporting To
The Cook will report directly to the Chef.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Prepare, season, cook and present a wide variety of dishes using different methods such as grilling, frying, roasting, boiling, steaming, and baking.
- Plan and coordinate food preparation activities to ensure timely service and consistent quality.
- Examine and inspect ingredients to ensure freshness, quality, and compliance with hygiene standards.
- Follow standardised recipes and portion control guidelines to maintain consistency across all dishes and control food costs.
- Regulate and monitor the temperature of ovens, grills, and other cooking equipment to achieve the required cooking results.
- Portion, arrange, and garnish dishes to ensure consistency and attractive presentation.
- Store food in temperature-controlled facilities and apply proper stock rotation (FIFO) to maintain freshness and minimise wastage.
- Assist in planning menus, estimating food requirements, and ordering supplies as needed.
- Adapt recipes and cooking methods to accommodate dietary requirements, allergies, special requests, or available ingredients.
- Supervise, mentor, and train kitchen assistants and apprentices in basic food preparation, safe work practices, and hygiene compliance.
- Maintain cleanliness and sanitation of kitchen areas, utensils, and equipment in accordance with food safety regulations and HACCP standards.
- Collaborate with chefs and other kitchen staff to ensure smooth operations, especially during peak service hours or catering functions.
- Monitor cooking processes, including timing and testing for doneness, to ensure food is cooked to safe internal temperatures and desired standards.
- Prepare foundational elements such as stocks, bases, or marinades to support menu items and enhance flavours during cooking.
- Inspect and organize kitchen inventory periodically to identify spoilage risks and support accurate food requirement estimations.
- Demonstrate and enforce safe handling practices for ingredients and equipment to apprentices, promoting compliance with hygiene protocols.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- AQF Certificate III
- A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience

Essential Skills
- Strong knowledge of food preparation methods, cooking techniques, and portion control.
- Ability to follow standardised recipes and adapt cooking methods when required.
- Good communication skills to collaborate effectively with colleagues and support smooth kitchen operations.
- Ability to supervise and provide on-the-job training for kitchen assistants and apprentices.
- Teamwork and training skills to guide junior staff and maintain a positive working environment.
- Capability to work efficiently under pressure in a fast-paced kitchen environment.
- Knowledge of food hygiene, safety practices, and HACCP compliance.
- Time management and organisational skills to coordinate multiple tasks and ensure timely service.
- Attention to detail in food presentation, portioning, and quality control.

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.

To learn more about our organisation visit monashhealth.org.

Monash Health is Victoria's largest and most comprehensive health service. For more than 170 years, Monash Health and its predecessors have provided safe, high-quality healthcare for people at every life stage. With 25,500 employees, we provide care to south-eastern metropolitan Melbourne and rural Victoria from over 40 locations, via telehealth, within local communities and in people's homes.


We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. At Monash Health we are relentless in our pursuit of excellence and work to our six guiding principles and our five ICare values.



About Monash Doctors 


To help grow your career, there are more than 1,900 Junior and 1,700 Senior Doctors at Monash Health in over 200 medical specialties. We offer unparallel opportunities in Victoria's largest & most clinically diverse teaching health service. 



Monash Health seeks expressions of interest from excellent medical practitioners for its adult mental health services. Monash Health has a consultant led service delivery model, where the consultant is available upfront to lead patient care in every setting of care, supervise juniors and be available for timely escalation of care.



About the Mental Health Program (MHP) at Monash Health


Monash Health is the largest public health service in Victoria, employing over 18,000 people across a range of specialities.


Monash Health MHP is the largest in Victoria, serving nearly 25% of the Victorian population. The MHP runs the largest psychiatric training program in Victoria with nearly 100 trainee registrars and 20 prevocational trainees. Clinical diversity is a hall mark of the services provided by the MHP - with services such as neuropsychiatry, antenatal and perinatal, psycho-oncology, acute and community psychiatry to old age psychiatry - services across the life span. 



About The Role


- Consultant Psychiatrist - 0.4 EFT
- Monash Gender Clinic


The role is based within Adult Psychiatry unit at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, Monash Health, providing clinical and medical leadership to a multidisciplinary team of clinicians working with patients and the peer support workforce. The role operates out of Monash Gender Clinic premises located at the Victorian Pride Centre, St Kilda.


In this position, the Consultant Psychiatrist will work closely with the patients and their families, managers-team leaders, clinicians, registrars-HMOs-Interns and the peer support workforce to ensure the provision of safe and effective care as well as assist with the efficient management of the relevant units. The Consultant Psychiatrist will also play an integral role in supporting medical, clinical and peer support staff and managing patient journeys in order to optimise timeliness of care and meeting organisational expectations of care (please refer to Monash Health's iCARE values and Strategic Plan). All positions are supported by relevant junior medical staffing.



About You


You are a recent or an experienced Consultant Psychiatrist or a Senior Registrar awaiting Fellowship.


You Are Also 
- committed to a leadership & mentoring role
- dedicated to safe best practice & quality care
- committed to delivering patient centred care & a patient advocacy
- enthusiastic, compassionate & able to work collaboratively
- excited to be accountable for and manage specific portfolios in our relentless pursuit of excellence
- keenly interested in teaching medical students and registrars


What You Need
- Relevant Qualification - Fellowship of the Royal Australian & New Zealand College of Psychiatrists (FRANZCP) or equivalent 
- Demonstrated experience
- Current AHPRA registration
- Participation in CPD
- Valid WWC certificate
- Valid Driving licence - senior medical staff are required to travel between Monash Health sites should the need arise
- Australian working rights


What We Offer
- access to Monash Health in-house learning portals 
- avenues to further develop your leadership skills
- mentorship 
- support to attend relevant forums & conferences
- a supportive learning environment, should you wish to undertake further training and studies, including a PhD in psychiatric subspecialties in collaboration with Monash University Department of Psychiatry


In addition, you will have access to benefits including salary packaging to increase your take-home pay, access to onsite staff car parking and gym, and the Employee Assistance Program (EAP).



For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Dr Vaidy Swaminathan, Head of Unit, Adult Psychiatry, MMC or Ms Natalie Cross, PA to HoU, Adult Psychiatry, MMC, on (03) 9594 7795. 



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.
